question.problem:
Consider the system of equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-3y+z=4 \\ y-4z=-6 \\ 3x+y+z=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}$, where $D$ is the determinant of the coefficient matrix and ${D}_{y}=$
question.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}1x+(-3)y+1z=4 \\ 0x+1y+(-4)z=-6 \\ 3x+1y+1z=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
D=|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & -6 & -4 \\ 3 & -8 & 1\end{aligned}|.
$$
